sections.title: Authority
sections.body: These rules govern referendums of the full membership. They may be amended only by referendum. No body may alter the referendum process except by referendum.
sections.rationale: The rules for direct member votes must be controlled by the members themselves, not by any delegated body.

sections.title: When Referendums Occur
sections.body: A referendum shall be held when: (1) a petition signed by 10% of members requests it, (2) the Assembly refers a question by two-thirds vote, (3) these rules or governing documents require it, (4) the Constitution or Charter requires it.
sections.rationale: Multiple paths to referendum prevent any single body from blocking member input. The 10% petition threshold is high enough to prevent frivolous votes but low enough to be achievable.

sections.title: Participation Requirement
sections.body: All referendums require participation from at least one-third (1/3) of eligible members to be valid. Referendums that do not meet this threshold are void.
sections.rationale: Low-turnout referendums create the risk that unrepresentative minorities make binding decisions. One-third participation is achievable but ensures meaningful member engagement.

sections.title: Simple Majority
sections.body: The following questions require a simple majority (more than half of votes cast) to pass: (1) amendments to the Charter, (2) amendments to the Assembly Rules, (3) general policy referendums, (4) recall of Assembly members or officers.
sections.rationale: Most referendum questions should require only majority support, not supermajorities that create minority veto power.

sections.title: Two-Thirds Majority
sections.body: The following questions require a two-thirds (2/3) majority of votes cast to pass: (1) amendments to the Constitution, (2) amendments to these Referendum Rules.
sections.rationale: Changes to the foundational documents and to the referendum process itself require broader consensus than ordinary policy questions.
